questions.stem: An AMI is best described as:
choices: A bootable disk image used to launch EC2 instances
questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image is the template (OS + pre-installed software) from which EC2 launches new instances.

questions.stem: Which EC2 instance family is best for an in-memory Redis cache?
questions.explanation: R-family instances have the highest RAM-to-vCPU ratio — ideal for in-memory caches and databases.

questions.stem: Which instance family suffix indicates a Graviton (Arm) CPU?
questions.explanation: A trailing `g` (e.g. m7g, c7g) denotes AWS Graviton Arm processors, typically ~20% cheaper than equivalent x86.

questions.stem: Spot Instances can be reclaimed with how much notice?
questions.explanation: AWS issues a 2-minute interruption notice via instance metadata or CloudWatch Events before reclaiming Spot capacity.

questions.stem: Which workload is the WORST fit for Spot Instances?
choices: Stateless web tier behind ASG with diversified instance pools
Primary production database with stateful data
questions.explanation: A stateful primary DB cannot tolerate sudden eviction. Spot is for fault-tolerant, stateless, or checkpointable workloads.

questions.stem: An Auto Scaling Group should use which health check type to replace instances whose application has crashed but the OS is still up?
questions.explanation: EC2 health checks only see VM-level failures. ELB health checks probe the application port/path, catching app-level crashes.

questions.stem: An ALB operates at which OSI layer?
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer is Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) — supports content-based routing, host/path rules, WebSocket, HTTP/2.

questions.stem: Which load balancer is appropriate for sub-millisecond TCP load balancing at millions of requests per second with static IPs?
questions.explanation: NLB is Layer 4, offers static IPs per AZ, and is built for extreme-scale TCP/UDP/TLS workloads.

questions.stem: What does a Compute Savings Plan apply to that an EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not?
choices: Across families, Regions, and even Fargate/Lambda
Only the same instance family in one Region
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans are broader (any family/Region, plus Fargate and Lambda) at a slightly smaller discount than the more restrictive EC2 Instance plan.

questions.stem: An ASG uses 'target tracking on CPU at 60%'. What happens at sustained 80% CPU?
choices: ASG launches more instances until average CPU returns near 60%
questions.explanation: Target tracking adds capacity to drive the metric back toward its target.

questions.stem: Where should session state be stored to make a web tier truly stateless?
choices: EBS volume attached to one instance
questions.explanation: External, shared state stores (DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Redis) let any instance serve any request and let the ASG replace instances freely.

questions.stem: User-data on EC2 is executed by default:
choices: Only on the first boot of the instance
Never; it must be enabled per launch
questions.explanation: By default, user-data runs on first boot only. You can opt in to per-boot execution but the default is one-shot.

questions.stem: An IAM role attached to an EC2 instance via an instance profile gives the application:
choices: Static IAM access keys hardcoded into the AMI
Temporary credentials via the instance metadata service
questions.explanation: The SDK reads temporary, auto-rotated credentials from IMDS; avoids hardcoding static access keys.

questions.stem: An ALB target group can target which of the following?
choices: EC2 instances, IP addresses, or Lambda functions
Only on-prem servers via Direct Connect
questions.explanation: ALB target groups support instances, raw IPs (including on-prem), and Lambda — enabling Lambda as a backend for HTTP.

questions.stem: Which scaling policy uses ML forecasting from historical metrics?
questions.explanation: Predictive scaling analyses historical load and pre-provisions capacity ahead of expected spikes.

questions.stem: A 'golden AMI' workflow is preferred because:
choices: AWS gives a discount on custom AMIs
Pre-baked AMIs boot fast and produce deterministic instances
Custom AMIs are required for ASGs
questions.explanation: Baking dependencies into the AMI cuts boot time and removes variability from user-data scripts.

questions.stem: An EC2 instance can be in which state during which billing pauses (for most instance types)?
questions.explanation: Stopped instances don't incur compute charges (EBS storage still bills). Running and even pending charge for compute.

questions.stem: Which AWS feature lets you SSH-equivalent into an instance without opening port 22 or managing key pairs?
questions.explanation: SSM Session Manager uses the SSM agent and IAM auth, eliminating the need for inbound SSH ports or key pair distribution.

questions.stem: Placement groups can be configured as:
questions.explanation: Cluster (low-latency, same AZ), Spread (each instance on distinct hardware), Partition (HDFS-style fault domains) are the three placement-group strategies.

questions.stem: An NLB provides:
choices: Static IPs per AZ via Elastic IPs
questions.explanation: NLB exposes a static IP per AZ, useful when clients can't follow DNS or need IP allow-lists. ALB does not.

questions.stem: What's the typical price relationship for the same workload?
questions.explanation: On-Demand is most expensive, then Reserved/Savings Plans, then Spot — Spot trades flexibility for the deepest discount.

questions.stem: What does the EC2 instance metadata service (IMDS) v2 require that v1 did not?
choices: A session token via PUT before GET (defends against SSRF)
questions.explanation: IMDSv2 mandates a short PUT-then-GET token exchange, mitigating SSRF attacks that proxied requests to 169.254.169.254.

questions.stem: An ASG spans 3 AZs with min=3, max=12, desired=6. One AZ goes dark. What happens?
choices: The ASG rebalances by launching replacement instances in the remaining healthy AZs
Scaling pauses until the AZ returns
Instances migrate live to the other AZs
questions.explanation: ASGs maintain desired capacity across remaining healthy AZs, launching replacements as needed.

questions.stem: Which compute service should you choose for tightly coupled MPI HPC workloads requiring lowest inter-node latency?
choices: EC2 with Cluster placement group + EFA
questions.explanation: Cluster placement plus Elastic Fabric Adapter delivers the low-latency, high-bandwidth networking MPI HPC requires.

questions.stem: Which is TRUE about Elastic IP addresses?
choices: They are free while associated with a running instance and charged when idle
questions.explanation: AWS charges for idle/unattached Elastic IPs to discourage hoarding; the first one is free while in active use.
